summary.whatChanges: In both Zod v4 classic and mini, `ZodEnum.options` is now built from the schema's internal parsed value set instead of `Object.values(def.entries)`. For numeric TypeScript enums, the reverse-mapping string keys no longer appear in `options`, which now matches exactly what parsing accepts. Tests were added for both variants.
behaviorChanges: z.enum(SomeNumericEnum).options no longer contains the reverse-mapping string keys (e.g. "Tuna"), only the numeric values
options now always matches the set of values the schema will accept at parse time
Same change applies to z.enum in zod/mini
Ordering of options now follows the internal values set rather than Object.values order
risks: Code that iterated options for numeric enums and expected both keys and values (e.g. building UI lists or docs) will now see half as many entries
Element order of options may differ from the previous Object.values order, affecting order-sensitive consumers or snapshot tests
The `as util.EnumValue[]` cast bypasses type checking of what _zod.values actually contains
Relies on _zod.values being populated before options is assigned during construction
